title: Applying News and Media Sentiment Analysis for Generating Forex Trading Signals

extraction.methodology_summary: The paper constructs sentiment scores from news articles and social media posts pertaining to the US Dollar (USD) using a lexicon-based approach (VADER) and a machine learning approach (Naïve Bayes). These sentiment scores are then combined with technical analysis indicators (moving average and relative strength index) on the H4 timeframe to generate Forex buy or sell trading signals.
extraction.universe: News articles from financial sources like Reuters and Bloomberg, and Twitter posts related to the US Dollar and major currency pairs

performance_metrics.context: Naïve Bayes model with MA and RSI confirmation over the testing period
performance_metrics.evidence_quote: With confirmation from the MA and RSI, the signals generated by the Naïve Bayes model showed that a profit of over 12% was gained over the testing period.

performance_metrics.context: Lexicon-based models with RSI and MA confirmation over the testing period
performance_metrics.evidence_quote: While the lexicon-based models using confirmation from the RSI and MA indicators generated a profit of 5% over the testing period.

performance_metrics.context: Naïve Bayes model sentiment classification accuracy
performance_metrics.evidence_quote: The accuracy of the Naïve Bayes model indicates that it correctly classified 85% of the news articles and social media posts as either neutral, negative, or positive sentiments.

key_findings: Combining sentiment analysis of news and social media with technical indicators (MA and RSI) generates profitable Forex trading signals.
The Naïve Bayes machine learning model outperforms the lexicon-based VADER approach in accuracy, precision, recall, and overall profitability.
Using the H4 timeframe cushions algorithmic reactions against sudden news events and helps mitigate slippage.
limitations: Sentiment analysis can sometimes be biased.
The system relies entirely on sentiment analysis which may not capture all market-driving factors.
